$comment: Brumista's protocol: every command it answers. The source of truth: the C++ dispatch table in src/BrumistaCommands.cpp is checked against it (tools/check-commands.sh), and the MCP server generates its tools from it (protocol/protocol.go embeds this file). Shapes use the notation of protocol/limen/commands.json: JSON values as type names, a key ending in ? may be absent, [T] is an array of T. limenDiff notes where a command departs from limen's; undo says what a write leaves in Rack's Edit > Undo.

transport.framing: one JSON object per line, newline-terminated, both ways; empty lines are ignored, a trailing \r is dropped
transport.clients: one at a time; a second connection waits for the first to close

the command's params, at the top level

ok.result: the command's result; null for commands that return nothing

transport.threads: commands marked main touch the engine or the scene: they are queued and run in Brumista's widget step(), on the main thread. The server thread waits 2 s. A command still queued when the wait ends is cancelled and never runs; one the main thread has started is waited for until it finishes. Commands marked server read plugin data that doesn't change while Rack runs.
limenDiff: Port 7200, not 7000.
Every read that touches the engine or the scene runs on the main thread; limen reads params, ports, cables and module info from the server thread.
A timed-out command is cancelled rather than left queued (limen problem late-timeout).
Every write records a Rack undo step, so Ctrl+Z works on it (limen problem undo).
A request line over 1 MiB closes the connection with "request too long".

commands.name: hello
commands.description: Brumista's version and the commands it supports. The version is the plugin's, which the protocol and the MCP binary share.
limenDiff: limen replies { protocol: 2, commands }; Brumista names itself and reports its semver version instead of an integer.

commands.name: list_plugins
commands.description: Every plugin loaded in Rack.

commands.name: list_models
commands.description: Every module model Rack can create, optionally for one plugin.

plugin.description: plugin slug; an unknown slug returns an empty list

commands.name: list_modules
commands.description: The modules in the patch, with grid position and width.

plugin.description: plugin slug; an unknown slug returns an empty list

commands.name: get_module
commands.description: One module, in the shape list_modules uses.
commands.result: same object as one list_modules entry

commands.name: get_module_info
commands.description: What Rack's right-click Info menu shows: model metadata, tags and the plugin's identity and links.

commands.name: list_ports
commands.description: A module's inputs and outputs by index, with their names, channel counts and instant voltages. A voltage is one sample taken when the call runs: good for held signals such as pitch CV, gates held open or offsets, meaningless for audio-rate or fast ones, and a short trigger is easily missed.

inputs.name: string, empty when the port has no name

outputs.name: string, empty when the port has no name

notes: Lists every port the engine module declares, including any with no jack on the panel.
voltages is always an array, empty when channels is 0, as on an unpatched input. Mono and poly have one shape.
The values in one reply are not one instant: the engine keeps running while they are read, so two fast signals can't be compared.
limenDiff: Adds channels and voltages, which limen doesn't report.

commands.name: list_params
commands.description: A module's parameters: current value, name, range, unit and default, the value as the module displays it, and a switch's labels.

result.value: number, raw, in min to max
result.display?: string, the value as the module's tooltip shows it, with its unit, e.g. "440.0 Hz" or a switch's label
labels?: string, a switch's label for each position, from min up

notes: value is the engine's current value, which glides toward a knob's target on a smoothed parameter; display shows the target, as Rack's tooltip does.
display comes from the module's own code; it is left out if that code fails.
A parameter is the knob's position, not what the module does with it once CV is added: that shows only at the outputs.
limenDiff: Adds default, display and labels, which limen doesn't report.

commands.name: get_param
commands.description: One parameter, in the shape list_params uses.
commands.result: same object as one list_params entry

commands.name: get_module_data
commands.description: A module's own saved state, read live: what its dataToJson() writes under "data" in the patch file. It holds what parameters don't, such as a quantizer's scale mask or a sequencer's steps, in a shape each module chooses.

result.data: any JSON the module writes; null when it keeps none

notes: The shape is the module's own and undocumented by Rack; the module's source or a saved .vcv shows what the keys mean.
Some modules store large data here, such as samples or long text, so the reply can be large.
limenDiff: New; limen has no such command.

commands.name: list_cables
commands.description: The cables in the patch with their colours, optionally only those touching one module.

id.description: only cables with this module at either end

result.color?: string, "#rrggbb" or "#rrggbbaa", from the cable's widget

limenDiff: Adds color, which limen doesn't report.

commands.name: set_param
commands.description: Set a parameter's value. The value is clamped to the parameter's range and rounded on stepped parameters, as turning the knob would; the reply reads it back.

value.description: new value, in the parameter's own range (list_params shows min and max)

commands.result: the parameter after the change, in the shape list_params uses
commands.undo: one step, only when the value changed
limenDiff: Runs on the main thread; limen writes from the server thread.
Clamps and snaps through the ParamQuantity; limen stores the raw value, so 12 on a 0 to 1 knob reads back as 12.
Returns the parameter; limen returns null.

commands.name: add_module
commands.description: Create a module and place it at a grid position, or next to an existing module when no position is given. Returns where it landed.

x.description: grid column in HP; give x and y together

y.description: rack row; give x and y together

mode.description: what to do when the position is taken: nearest moves to the closest free place, force pushes neighbours in the row aside, squeeze slides them to make room, strict refuses

errors: x and y must both be numbers
unknown mode (expected nearest, force, squeeze, or strict)
commands.undo: one step: the new module, with any modules force or squeeze pushed aside
limenDiff: An unknown mode is refused before the module is created; limen creates it, then removes it.

commands.name: remove_module
commands.description: Remove a module and its cables, as Rack's Delete does.
errors: Brumista can't remove a Brumista module
commands.undo: one step: the cables, the module, and the gap closed when Rack's squeeze setting is on
limenDiff: Goes through Rack's Delete, so with squeeze on the modules to the right close the gap; limen leaves it.
Refuses to remove a Brumista module, which would stop the server answering the call.

commands.name: move_module
commands.description: Move a module to a grid position and report where it landed.

mode.description: what to do when the position is taken: nearest moves to the closest free place, force pushes neighbours in the row aside, squeeze slides them to make room, strict refuses

errors: unknown mode (expected nearest, force, squeeze, or strict)
commands.undo: one step for every module that moved; none when nothing moved
notes: Every mode but strict may land the module somewhere other than x, y. Fractional positions snap to the grid.

commands.name: add_cable
commands.description: Connect an output to an input with a coloured cable. Without a colour, the cable takes Rack's next cable colour, as a dragged cable does.
errors: missing outputModule, outputPort, inputModule, or inputPort
color must be a string "#rrggbb" or "#rrggbbaa"
output port has no jack on the panel
input port has no jack on the panel
notes: An input may take more than one cable; Rack sums them, as with stacked cables.
limenDiff: Refuses a port the panel has no jack for (limen problem panel-jack, which crashed Rack).
Returns the cable's colour as well as its id.

commands.name: remove_cable
commands.description: Remove a cable.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Run a list of commands in order in one round trip. The whole batch is one step in Rack's Edit > Undo.
request objects, each with its own cmd and params, as they would be sent alone

stopOnError.description: stop after the first failing command

result.count: integer, commands that ran, the failing one included
result.stopped?: integer, index of the command that stopped the batch
results: each command's own reply, { ok, result } or { ok, error }

commands.undo: one step for the whole batch, holding the steps of every command that ran; none when nothing changed
notes: The envelope is ok whenever the batch is well formed; failures are inside results.
A nested batch is refused inside results with "batch cannot be nested", and a non-object entry with "command must be an object".
Commands that ran before a failure stay done; Ctrl+Z takes them back together.
A stopOnError that isn't a boolean is ignored, as in limen.
limenDiff: Runs as one main-thread task, so no frame falls between its commands; limen sends each write to the main thread on its own. The 2 s wait covers the batch's start, not its length.
The whole batch is one undo step (limen problem undo).

commands.name: save_patch
commands.description: Save the patch to its own file, as Rack's Save does. With a path, write a copy there instead and leave the patch's file alone.

path.description: absolute path for a copy; .vcv is added when missing

overwrite.description: replace the file at path if one exists

errors: patch has never been saved; use save_patch_as with a path
file exists; set overwrite to replace it
notes: Without a path the patch is marked saved, as Rack's Save marks it. A copy leaves the patch's unsaved state as it was, and the copy itself opens as saved.
Inside a batch, the batch's own undo step lands after the save, so Rack shows the patch as changed although the file holds the batch's edits.
limenDiff: A copy refuses to replace an existing file unless overwrite is true; limen overwrites without asking.
Relative paths and missing folders are refused; .vcv is added when missing, as Rack's Save as does.
limen leaves the patch marked unsaved and writes that mark into the file.

commands.name: save_patch_as
commands.description: Rack's Save as: write the patch to path and make it the patch's own file. Refuses to replace an existing file unless overwrite is true.

path.description: absolute path; .vcv is added when missing

overwrite.description: replace the file at path if one exists

errors: file exists; set overwrite to replace it
notes: The patch is marked saved, its folder becomes Rack's last patch folder, and the file joins File > Open recent, as with Rack's Save as.
limenDiff: Refuses to replace an existing file unless overwrite is true; limen overwrites without asking.
Relative paths and missing folders are refused; .vcv is added when missing, as Rack's Save as does.
limen leaves the patch marked unsaved and writes that mark into the file.

commands.name: set_fullscreen
commands.description: Enter or leave fullscreen; reports the resulting state.
commands.undo: none; the window isn't part of the patch

commands.name: zoom_to_modules
commands.description: Fit the view to all modules, as Rack's F4 does.
commands.undo: none; the view isn't part of the patch
notes: Fits once before replying and again over the next two frames: a single fit sets the zoom, but the scroll offset is clamped against the old view until the scroll area catches up. limen also zooms over three frames.
